tasks.short: Use radiation safety measures and protection devices.

steps.what: Read the protection card for this exam before the exposure.
Use radiation safety measures and protection devices to comply with government regulations and to ensure the safety of patients and staff.

tasks.design: A protection card lists the exam name, the view, and the shield or distance rule. A lead technologist writes it before the exposure. The radiologic technologist reads it, then still places the protection on the patient. If the card has no row, the technologist reads the paper protocol in the same step.
tasks.previous_blocker: The shield rule sat in a long paper protocol the technologist hunted while the patient waited.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper card with the exam name, the view, and the shield or distance rule is enough. No new software is required.
tasks.still_hard: Placing the protection on this patient, and judging whether the rule fits this body and this view, stays with the technologist.
tasks.human_edge: The technologist sees the patient and decides how the protection sits.
tasks.altitude: The technologist still applies the protection. The card only shortens finding the rule.

reach.task: Apply the same protection rule on a treatment setup
reach.learn: Read the exam name, the view, and the shield or distance rule, then still place the protection.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the exam name, the view, and the shield or distance rule shortens the search when the row is there. The technologist still places the protection. Model knowledge.

Ionising radiation is a reserved act, and others act only on assignment with instructions. The radiologic technologist still applies the protection devices. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited act.
Medical-purpose software is a device under the cited regulation. This paper card is not software. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited regulation.

assumptions: A lead technologist writes the protection card before the exposure.
Fields are the exam name, the view, and the shield or distance rule.
The card does not name a diagnosis and does not place the protection.
If the row is missing, the radiologic technologist reads the paper protocol inside s1.
There is no native system to configure and no custom code.
Focal upkeep is zero because the lead technologist keeps the card, counted on the other line.
Works-council consultation for a monitoring or scoring system is out of scope because this design adds none.
Ionising radiation stays a reserved act the radiologic technologist performs.
unknowns: Whether this department already keeps a one-page protection card for each exam.
research_questions: How often a new exam has no row on the protection card.

incremental.description: No extra technologist upkeep. The lead technologist keeps the protection card.
The lead technologist writes the protection card: exam name, view, and shield or distance rule.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The exam is new, so the protection card has no row and the technologist reads the paper protocol. The search saving disappears.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Operate the picture archive for each study.

steps.what: Read the study card before this archive lookup.
Operate the digital picture archiving communications systems.

tasks.design: A study card lists the study number, the exam, and the one folder. A medical records specialist writes it before the lookup. The radiologic technologist reads it, then still operates the digital picture archive on {OTHER}. If the card has no row, the technologist reads the paper request in the same step.
tasks.previous_blocker: The study number and the folder sat on the paper request, and the technologist hunted the right folder on the archive screen.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper card with the study number, the exam, and the one folder is enough. The archive itself is unchanged.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the right study, and storing or retrieving it on the archive, stays with the technologist. A wrong folder can attach images to the wrong patient.
tasks.human_edge: The technologist matches the person in the room to the study before storing or retrieving it.
tasks.altitude: The technologist still operates the archive. The card only shortens finding the folder.

reach.task: Write the study number and the folder before imaging
reach.learn: The card fields are the study number, the exam, and the one folder. The technologist still operates the archive.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the study number, the exam, and the one folder shortens the search when the row is there. The technologist still operates the archive. Model knowledge.
The medical dossier is kept for 20 years, and a patient may ask who viewed it. This card does not replace that dossier. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited page.
Health data are a special category. The study stays health data in the dossier. This design adds no automated processing of it. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited article.

assumptions: A medical records specialist writes the study card before the technologist operates the archive.
Fields are the study number, the exam, and the one folder.
The card does not store or retrieve the study and does not name a diagnosis.
If the row is missing, the radiologic technologist reads the paper request inside s1.
The archive on {OTHER} is the picture archive already in use. There is no new link and no custom code.
Focal upkeep is zero because the medical records specialist keeps the card, counted on the other line.
Works-council consultation for a monitoring or scoring system is out of scope because this design adds none.
unknowns: Whether this department already writes the study number and the folder on one card.
research_questions: How often an add-on view has no row on the study card.

incremental.description: No extra technologist upkeep. The medical records specialist keeps the study card.
The medical records specialist writes the study card: study number, exam, and one folder.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The study card has no row for an add-on view, so the technologist reads the paper request. The search saving disappears.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take thorough and accurate patient medical histories.

steps.what: Read the known-item card before this patient history.
Take thorough and accurate patient medical histories.
Write the spoken history into the dossier after the interview.

tasks.design: A known-item card lists the exam name and one item a nurse already wrote, not the full history and not a diagnosis. The nurse writes it before the interview. The radiologic technologist reads it, then still takes the history with the patient and still writes that history into the dossier. If the card has no row, the technologist reads the paper request in the same step.
tasks.previous_blocker: The one known item sat on the paper request, and the technologist hunted it before asking the patient.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper card with the exam name and one known item is enough. No new software is required.
tasks.still_hard: The patient tells an unstructured history. The technologist still has to ask, listen, and write what is accurate.
tasks.human_edge: The technologist hears what the patient will not put on a card, and decides what belongs in the history.
tasks.altitude: The technologist still takes the history and still writes it. The card only shortens finding the one known item.

reach.task: Write the one known item before imaging
reach.learn: The card fields are the exam name and one known item. The technologist still takes the history.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the exam name and one known item shortens the search when the row is there. The technologist still takes the history and still writes it. Model knowledge.
The medical dossier is kept for 20 years. This card does not replace that dossier, and the written history stays in it. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited page.
Health data are a special category. The spoken history stays health data in the dossier. This design adds no automated processing of it. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited article.

Recording a consultation or logging corrections can count as staff monitoring under the cited works-council article. This paper card does neither. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited article.

assumptions: A registered nurse writes the known-item card before the interview.
Fields are the exam name and one known item the nurse already wrote.
The card is not the history and does not name a diagnosis.
If the row is missing, the radiologic technologist reads the paper request inside s1.
The spoken history is produced in s2, and s3 writes that history.
There is no native system to configure and no custom code.
Focal upkeep is zero because the nurse keeps the card, counted on the other line.
Works-council consultation for a monitoring or scoring system is out of scope because this design adds none.
unknowns: Whether the nurse already writes one known item on the imaging request.
research_questions: How often a first visit has no row on the known-item card.

incremental.description: No extra technologist upkeep. The nurse keeps the known-item card.
The nurse writes the known-item card: exam name and one known item.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A first visit has no row on the known-item card, so the technologist reads the paper request. The search saving disappears.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Make exposures and repeat work that misses the standard.

steps.what: Read the exposure card for the requested procedure.
Make the exposures necessary for the requested procedures, rejecting and repeating work that does not meet established standards.

tasks.design: An exposure card lists the procedure, the view, and the established standard that says when a view fails. A lead technologist writes it before the exposure. The radiologic technologist reads it, then still makes the exposure and still rejects and repeats work that misses that standard. If the card has no row, the technologist reads the paper standard in the same step.
tasks.previous_blocker: The repeat standard sat in a long paper protocol the technologist hunted at the console.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper card with the procedure, the view, and the fail rule is enough. No new software is required.
tasks.still_hard: Making the exposure, and judging whether this image meets the standard, stays with the technologist.
tasks.human_edge: The technologist sees the patient and the image together and decides whether to reject and repeat.
tasks.altitude: The technologist still makes the exposure and still rejects and repeats it. The card only shortens finding the standard.

reach.task: State which view fails the standard
reach.learn: The card fields are the procedure, the view, and the fail rule. The technologist still rejects and repeats the exposure.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the procedure, the view, and the fail rule shortens the search when the row is there. The technologist still makes, rejects, and repeats the exposure. Model knowledge.

Ionising radiation is a reserved act, and others act only on assignment with instructions. The radiologic technologist still makes the exposure. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited act.

Medical-device rules sit in the cited annex, and AI covered there is high-risk when a notified body must assess it. This paper card is not such a system. Model knowledge of this design; the rules are the cited annex and article.

assumptions: A lead technologist writes the exposure card before the exposure.
Fields are the procedure, the view, and the established standard that says when a view fails.
The card does not make the exposure and does not name a diagnosis.
If the row is missing, the radiologic technologist reads the paper standard inside s1.
There is no native system to configure and no custom code.
Focal upkeep is zero because the lead technologist keeps the card, counted on the other line.
Works-council consultation for a monitoring or scoring system is out of scope because this design adds none.
Ionising radiation stays a reserved act the radiologic technologist performs.
unknowns: Whether this department already keeps a one-page fail rule for each procedure.
research_questions: How often an uncommon procedure has no row on the exposure card.

incremental.description: No extra technologist upkeep. The lead technologist keeps the exposure card.
The lead technologist writes the exposure card: procedure, view, and the fail rule.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: An uncommon procedure has no row on the exposure card, so the technologist reads the paper standard. The search saving disappears.

role.altitude: The technologist still applies the protection, operates the archive, takes the history, and makes or repeats the exposure. A card only shortens finding the shield rule, the study folder, the known item, or the repeat standard.
reach: A radiation therapist can read the protection card and still places the protection.
A medical records specialist writes the study number and the folder, and the technologist still operates the archive.
A registered nurse writes the one known item, and the technologist still takes the history.
A radiologist states the fail rule, and the technologist still rejects and repeats the exposure.
skills_to_grow: Open the paper protocol, the paper request, or the paper standard when the card has no row.
Decide the protection, the folder, the history, and the repeat from the patient and the image, not from the card.
role.ambitious_version: Cards do not shield the patient, operate the archive, take the history, or make the exposure. The technologist still does.
